title: Quantitative Measurement of Conservative and Dissipative Shear Forces Using Quartz Tuning Fork Probes
content: Precise force measurements at the nanoscale are essential for advancing our understanding of tip-sample interactions in atomic force microscopy (AFM). Quartz tuning fork (QTF) sensors have emerged as a powerful alternative to traditional AFM cantilevers, offering high stiffness, a high quality factor, and an intrinsic piezoelectric response [1]. However, the coupled oscillation behavior of QTF prongs complicates the extraction of quantitative force measurements, particularly in distinguishing between conservative and dissipative interactions. In this study, we present an experimental and theoretical framework for measuring noncontact shear forces between silicon surfaces across single- and sub-nanometer gaps using QTF sensors. We employ the center-of-mass (COM) damper model to decouple intrinsic sensor dissipation from tip-sample interaction dissipation, enabling accurate extraction of conservative and dissipative force components [2].
